title: River Witham sword blade inscription (British Museum 1858,1116.5)

documents.route: unknown (inlaid on one face of a sword blade found in the River Witham near Lincoln, 1825)

plaintext.source: No reading exists that is accepted; Winter 2016/2026 is one unverified proposal.

transcription.source: British Library Medieval manuscripts blog, 3 Aug 2015 (J. Harrison); Winter, Waffen- und Kostuemkunde 58/2 (2016); checked 11 Nov 2026 (Brice Dudout) on two British Museum photographs: the BL blog inscription detail ('courtesy of the British Museum') and BM collection image 00296785 (not reproduced)
transcription.notes: #10 read as uncial N and #11 as C (BL 2015: R, G); the Stamford Mercury of 18 Aug 1826 (quoted by Rob Wheeler) and van Hasselt 2015 have N and C there. #17 V (or Y) and #18 I (or N, against the final cross) uncertain. Details: dudout/TRANSCRIPTION.md.

system.summary: Eighteen capital letters inlaid in gold wire between two crosses; no word division; system unknown (abbreviation or initials inscription is one proposal, not shown).
system.notes: Vowels O, O, I are 3 of 18 letters (about 17%), far below Latin running text; fits initials or abbreviations, shown by count only. W is not a Latin letter. Letter order matches the SDX invocation family of Wagner et al. 2009: longest common subsequence with Fyris UMF/B 74 13 of 18 letters (p 0.0002 against 5000 shuffles, 0.004 after Bonferroni over 18 siblings), with Marburg 11 of 18 (p 0.0012, 0.02 corrected); controls null (dudout/README.md).

prior_solution.where: Winter (Waffen- und Kostuemkunde 58/2, 2016, revised 2026-03-13) proposes an initials reading; the British Library (2015) called it indecipherable. Not accepted by a consensus.

conditions.human_role: Set the goal "solve the cipher from the Witham Sword"; no target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: British Library appeal (2015), Language Log and Cipher Mysteries threads, Winter 2016/2026: about twenty proposals, none verified.
Letter counts: vowels 3 of 18, D x3, X x3; points to initials or abbreviations, not running text.
Sibling inscribed blades (Alphen aan den Rijn, Berlin, Swedish): their own readings are speculative, so none supplies a key.
Judged Winter's initials reading: coherent but each expansion (X = CH, W a name) is chosen to fit; 18 letters cannot test it.

Read #10 as uncial N and #11 as C with curled upper terminal on two British Museum photographs (not reproduced); agrees with the Stamford Mercury of 18 Aug 1826 and with van Hasselt 2015. New reading +NDXOXCHWDNCHDXORVI+ (dudout/TRANSCRIPTION.md).

Longest common subsequence with 18 published sibling inscriptions (Wagner et al. 2009) against 5000 shuffles of the Witham letters: Fyris 74 13/18 p 0.0002, Marburg 11/18 p 0.0012 (Bonferroni x18: 0.004, 0.02); same with the BL 2015 reading (Fyris 74 p 0.0008); controls (Ulfberht, IN NOMINE DOMINI, GICELIN, HOMO DEI, INGELRII, St Benedict medal, laudes initials, Witham reversed) p 0.3-1.0. Shows family membership, not a reading.
Contiguous runs of initials / nomina sacra against 44 Latin prayers and formulas: best run 3 letters, p 0.73 against 1000 shuffles: not the acrostic of a known prayer.

outcome.method_basis: Eighteen letters with no key, clear copy or plaintext: any abbreviation expansion fits after the fact, and the sibling blades are themselves unread.
outcome.notes: Only route: read the inscribed-sword family together (needs photographs and the Wagner/Worley catalogue). 11 Nov 2026 (Brice Dudout): transcription corrected at #10-11 (removes the 'R(e)g(em)' / DRGHD basis of Winter 2016 and others); family membership measured; the expansions of the family elements (DX = Dominus Christus, O invocative, EH(R)) remain Wagner et al.'s conjecture, and no expansion of Witham is testable.
